correctness.limitations: The finite replay certifies the two witness trees, not the general recurrence; the proof covers arbitrary labelled simple trees and fixed integer totals, not transient basins or cyclic graphs. The frozen script and log were inspected, not treated as independent evidence.
correctness.rationale: The tree incidence matrix is injective on edge fluxes (successively remove leaves). Hence F²(x)=x is equivalent to exact reversal of every edge sign. For a parent-child sign t and fluxes q,q′ the gap is zero only if q=q′, or tk with 1≤k≤t(q−q′)−1. On a tree these gap choices integrate uniquely up to translation, and the coefficient extraction enforces q=s+sum(t). The weight z^(−m_w tk) records the child's subtree contribution to total modulo n. Each residue-matching gap configuration has one lift to a specified integer total S; F preserves S, and the only fixed configurations are constant. This gives the subtraction and division by two, including n=1. The scalar transfer costs at most O(nΔ³) exact operations (n=1 separately); width-n cyclic arrays and at most O(Δ) monomial shifts per edge-weight entry fit the stated O(n³Δ³) bound. Coefficient lengths are polynomial because each edge has O(Δ) gaps. The independent direct two-update replay matches both six-vertex vectors and totals. Up to five vertices, each feasible tree degree multiset specifies a unique shape (paths, stars and the unique five-vertex tree with degrees 1,1,1,2,3).
